To deposit the compact TiO2 layer, 60 mL of a titanium diisopropoxide bis(acetylacetonate)/ethanol (with 1:10 volume ratio) solution was applied by spraying. After completing the spray pyrolysis step, the substrates were stored at 450  C for 1 h to improve the electrical properties, 74 then slowly cooled to room temperature. On top of the c -TiO2 layer, a mesoporous TiO2 (mp-TiO2) layer was deposited by spin-coating. The TiO2 paste, approximately 50 nm in diameter, was purchased from ShareChem. The paste was dispersed in ethanol/terpineol (78:22 w/w). The FTO/ c -TiO2 substrates prepared with mp-TiO2 were heated at 500  C on a hot plate for 1 h to remove organic compounds and then slowly cooled to 200  C.

To fabricate perovskite solar cells, the perovskite precursor solution was prepared by mixing 1,139 mg mL -1 FAPbI3 in a mixture of DMF and DMSO in a 4:1 ratio by volume. MACl was added in the range 0  50 mol%. For each sample, 70 m L of the filtered solution was spread over the FTO/ c -TiO2/mp-TiO2 substrate at 6,000 rpm for 50 s with 0.1 s ramping. During spin coating, 1 mL diethyl ether was dripped after spinning for 10 s using a pipette. The film was dried on a hot plate at 150  C for 10 min. After cooling the substrate, the perovskite film was spin coated with phenylethylammonium iodide (PEAI) dissolved with IPA (5 mM) at 3,000 rpm.

unresolved_notes: MACl, FACl, and MAI labels are additive-processing arms. Although MA substitution for FA is reported for the MACl series, exact finished bulk absorber formulae are not reported for every concentration. The evidence therefore does not support reliably splitting these concentration arms into separate composition-defined device families; they are retained as specimen variants within one reported stack.

The reported MA-ion substitution for FA and absence of anion-site Cl substitution cannot be assigned family-wide without incorrectly applying those MACl-arm findings to pristine, FACl, and MAI specimens. The schema has no group-only composition-claim record, so this distinction remains unresolved rather than being written into one universal absorber formula.

The 24.02% Table S3 MA-40 device and the 23.48% Newport-certified best device are kept as separate individual devices because the supplied evidence does not establish that they are the same physical specimen.

The Table S3 J-V outcomes do not identify whether each row is from the reverse or forward scan, although the methods report both protocols. Their scan_direction is therefore not_reported. The plotted forward/reverse curves contain no extractable numeric outcomes and were not digitized.

The methods report Class AAA solar-simulator measurement at 100 mA cm -2 under AM 1.5 G, no pre-scan light soaking, and a 100 mV step voltage. The schema has no dedicated performance-observation condition field, and these method-level conditions were not inserted as outcome metrics or used to infer a scan direction for the table rows.

The stabilized steady-state-current passage reports a maximum-power-point voltage of 0.98 V and a duration of 100 min but no current, power, efficiency, or other stabilized outcome. No stabilized-power-output observation was created, and these protocol values were not treated as intrinsic device properties.
The EQE passage states that integrated Jsc was shown but supplies no numeric integrated-current result, so no EQE-integrated-current observation was created.

The room-temperature storage specimen's additive arm is not identified in the supplied text. The thermal and photostability comparisons are linked only to the shared family and their reported pristine and MA-40 arms, not to the Table S3 physical devices.
Photostability humidity is reported as both 25% relative humidity in the results and below 30% RH in the methods; both source distinctions are preserved.
The FACl 10 mol% Voc is preserved exactly as reported as 7.039 V despite its anomalous appearance; it was not corrected.

The certified table contains parser-corrupted uncertainty symbols for efficiency and M and lacks an explicit sign before the Isc uncertainty. Those strings are preserved as reported rather than silently regularized.

The pristine, MA-10, MA-20, MA-30, MA-40, and MA-50 films used only for structural, morphological, compositional, and photophysical characterization, including the MA-40 annealing-time series, were excluded as photovoltaic device records.
